quests.instruction: Write the number 1: a short flag, then a straight line down.
quests.hint: Start with a tiny slant going down-left, then pull a straight line from the top down to the baseline.
quests.explanation: 1 is a standing line with a little flag. The flag keeps it from looking like a lowercase l or a capital I.
quests.funFact: The number 1 is neither a prime number nor a composite number.

quests.instruction: Write the number 4: a slant, a bar, and a standing line that crosses the bar.
quests.hint: Slant down to the left, then go across to the right. Lift your pen and pull a straight line down on the right, through the bar.
quests.explanation: 4 is made of straight strokes only. The standing line should cross the bar about two-thirds of the way along.
quests.funFact: Many clocks with Roman numerals show four as IIII instead of IV.

quests.instruction: Write 1 and 4 side by side. Make them the same height.
quests.hint: Both numbers reach the top line and sit on the baseline. Leave a gap about as wide as a finger.
quests.explanation: Numbers should be as tall as capital letters and the same height as each other.
quests.funFact: The digits we use are called Hindu-Arabic numerals, because they began in India and spread through the Arab world.

quests.instruction: Write the number 7: a bar across the top, then a slant down to the baseline.
quests.hint: Draw the top bar from left to right. Without lifting, slant down toward the bottom left.
quests.explanation: 7 is a bar and a slant, joined at a sharp corner. The slant should end on the baseline.
quests.funFact: A week has seven days.

quests.instruction: Write 1 and 7 together. Make it easy to tell them apart.
quests.hint: 1 has a small flag and is a straight stem. 7 has a bar across the top and a slanting stem.
quests.explanation: 1 and 7 can look alike when written fast. The flag on 1 and the bar on 7 are the clues.
quests.funFact: In some countries, people write 1 with a long flag and 7 with a crossbar so they can't be confused.

quests.instruction: Write 7, 4 and 1 in a row. All three are made of straight strokes.
quests.hint: Plan each shape's start point. Leave equal gaps and keep all on the baseline.
quests.explanation: Three numbers made of straight lines. Sharp corners and clear lines matter.
quests.funFact: A rainbow is traditionally said to have seven colors.

quests.instruction: Write the number 0: a tall oval, starting at the top and going to the left.
quests.hint: Start at the top, curve left and down, around the bottom and up. Close the oval where you began.
quests.explanation: 0 is taller than it is wide, which tells it apart from the letter O, which is rounder.
quests.funFact: Indian mathematicians treated zero as a number in its own right. Brahmagupta wrote rules for using it in the year 628.

quests.instruction: Write the number 6: a curve down from the top, then a loop at the bottom.
quests.hint: Start at the top right, curve left and down, then keep going around the bottom and close the loop in the middle.
quests.explanation: 6 is a curve that closes into a loop. The loop is at the bottom, and the tail curves up from the top.
quests.funFact: A cube has six faces.

quests.instruction: Write 0 and 6 together. Both are made with curves.
quests.hint: 0 is a closed oval, 6 has a loop on the bottom half. Both start at the top and go left.
quests.explanation: Both numbers use the counter-clockwise motion you know from the letter o.
quests.funFact: The word 'zero' comes through Italian from an Arabic word meaning 'empty'.

quests.instruction: Write the number 9: a circle at the top with a straight tail down.
quests.hint: Make a small circle at the top, going left from the top. Then pull a straight line down from its right side to the baseline.
quests.explanation: 9 is like the letter g, a circle with a tail. The circle is in the top half and the tail drops straight to the baseline.
quests.funFact: A well-known saying is that a cat has nine lives.

quests.instruction: Write the number 8: two loops, one on top of the other.
quests.hint: Start at the top right, curve left and down, cross over in the middle, curve around the bottom and come back up to the start.
quests.explanation: 8 is two loops stacked up. The top loop should be a little smaller than the bottom one.
quests.funFact: A spider has eight legs.

quests.instruction: Write 6, 9, 8 and 0 in a row. All four have loops.
quests.hint: 6 has its loop at the bottom, 9 has its loop at the top, 8 has two, 0 has one big oval. Keep all the same height.
quests.explanation: Four rounded numbers with loops in different places. Choose the loop position before you write.
quests.funFact: The infinity symbol, ∞, looks like an 8 lying on its side.

quests.instruction: Write the number 2: a curve at the top, a slant down, and a bar along the bottom.
quests.hint: Start at the left, curve up and over to the right, slant down to the bottom left, then slide along the baseline to the right.
quests.explanation: 2 has a curve and a flat bottom. The slant joins the curve to the baseline.
quests.funFact: A bicycle has two wheels.

quests.instruction: Write the number 3: two bumps, one on top of the other.
quests.hint: Start at the top left, curve right and around to the middle, then curve again around to the bottom left.
quests.explanation: 3 is two curves stacked, with the second one a little bigger. It is like a backwards letter E made of curves.
quests.funFact: A traffic light has three colors: red, amber and green.

quests.instruction: Write 2 and 3 side by side. Both start with a curve at the top.
quests.hint: 2 slants and ends with a flat base. 3 has two curves and no flat line. Keep them the same height.
quests.explanation: Both numbers begin the same way but end differently. Checking the end of each shows which one you are writing.
quests.funFact: The number 2 is the only even prime number.

quests.instruction: Write the number 5: a short stem, a round belly, and a flat bar on top.
quests.hint: Pull down a short line from the top, curve around to the right in a belly, then come back to the left. Add the flat top bar last.
quests.explanation: 5 is a short stem plus a belly. Adding the top bar at the end means you see the whole shape first.
quests.funFact: A starfish usually has five arms.

quests.instruction: Write 5 and 2 together. Show the different bottoms.
quests.hint: 5 ends in a curved belly and 2 ends in a flat bar. Check the base of each.
quests.explanation: 5 and 2 look different at the bottom. The belly of 5 and the flat base of 2 are the clues.
quests.funFact: A hand has five fingers.

quests.instruction: Write 3, 5 and 2 in a row. Keep the same height and equal gaps.
quests.hint: Three curvy numbers in a row. Leave gaps about a finger wide and keep every number the same height.
quests.explanation: Curvy numbers take more control than straight ones. Equal sizes show your hand is steady.
quests.funFact: A pentagon is a shape with five sides.

quests.instruction: Write the first three numbers: 0, 1, 2, in order.
quests.hint: Say 'zero, one, two' as you write. Keep numbers the same height, with equal gaps.
quests.explanation: Counting while writing helps you remember the order of numbers and their shapes.
quests.funFact: Computers use only two digits, 0 and 1, in a system called binary.

quests.instruction: Write the next two numbers: 3 and 4.
quests.hint: 3 has two curves, 4 has a slant and a standing line. Make both reach the top line.
quests.explanation: Writing two numbers with different structure checks your shapes. The curvy 3 and straight 4 are very different.
quests.funFact: Four-leaf clovers are rare, which is why people call them lucky.

quests.instruction: Write the numbers from 0 to 4 in order.
quests.hint: Plan your space: five numbers need small gaps and a steady height.
quests.explanation: Five numbers in a row is practice for longer numbers. Keep every digit at the same height.
quests.funFact: We count in tens, probably because we have ten fingers.

quests.instruction: Write 5, 6 and 7 in order.
quests.hint: 5 has a belly, 6 has a loop, 7 has a bar and slant. Check each shape before moving on.
quests.explanation: Three numbers, three different kinds of strokes: curve, loop and straight. Your hand needs to switch quickly.
quests.funFact: A standard die has six faces, numbered one to six.

quests.instruction: Write 8 and 9 in order.
quests.hint: 8 is two stacked loops, 9 is a circle with a tail. Make them the same height.
quests.explanation: Both numbers have loops. Starting each at the top is the key.
quests.funFact: An octopus has eight arms.

quests.instruction: Write the numbers from 5 to 9 in order.
quests.hint: Plan the row first. Keep all numbers on the baseline and the same height.
quests.explanation: Five different shapes in a row is a good workout. The loops should be the same size.
quests.funFact: Multiples of nine have digits that add up to nine, such as 18, because 1 + 8 = 9.

quests.instruction: Write all ten digits in order, from 0 to 9.
quests.hint: Say the numbers quietly as you write. Check the height and spacing every few numbers.
quests.explanation: Ten digits are all you need to write any number. Writing them in order shows that you know every shape.
quests.funFact: The ten digits from 0 to 9 can make every number there is.

quests.instruction: Write a countdown: 9 down to 0.
quests.hint: Count backwards in your head. Start with 9 and finish with 0, keeping every digit the same size.
quests.explanation: Writing numbers backwards makes you recall each shape without leaning on the usual order.
quests.funFact: Rocket launches use a countdown to zero.

quests.instruction: Write the even numbers: 0, 2, 4, 6, 8.
quests.hint: Jump by twos as you write. Check that each number sits on the baseline.
quests.explanation: Even numbers skip a number each time. Writing them reinforces counting as well as shapes.
quests.funFact: Even numbers can be shared equally between two people, and zero counts as even.

quests.instruction: Write 6 and 9. They look almost like each other upside down.
quests.hint: 6 has its loop at the bottom, 9 has its loop at the top. Say 'bottom loop, top loop'.
quests.explanation: Numbers that look like each other turned around are easy to mix up. Always check where the loop is.
quests.funFact: If you turn a 6 upside down, it looks like a 9.

quests.instruction: Write 3 and 8. Both have curves on the right.
quests.hint: 3 is open on the left, 8 is closed into two loops. Take care to close the loops.
quests.explanation: The difference is closing the loops. 8 is closed, 3 is not.
quests.funFact: The digit 8 is made of two loops, and it is the only digit with two closed loops.

quests.instruction: Write 1, 7, 4 and 9 in a row. Each has a straight line.
quests.hint: 1 is a flag and a stem, 7 is a bar and slant, 4 is a slant, bar and stem, and 9 is a circle and stem.
quests.explanation: Four numbers that use straight lines. Make the stems straight and the same height.
quests.funFact: A calculator builds each digit out of seven small bars.
